item.text: The first day spent $59.01 and delivered 27 link clicks. The “Bracket busted” post has the early cost advantage—about $1.86 per click versus $2.66—but the sample is still small. I’ll keep both running for another day before shifting the budget.

After two days, “Bracket busted” is still delivering link clicks about 30% more cheaply. I’ve shifted the daily split to $40 for that post and $20 for the full-details post. Their combined lifetime caps remain $550. Entries aren’t visible in X, so this decision is based on click cost.

Going into Final Four weekend, the campaign has spent $222.57 for 108 link clicks. “Bracket busted” still has the lower click cost, at about $1.83 versus $2.60. I’m increasing daily budgets to $85 and $25 respectively to make the remaining $327.43 available across the final three days. The $550 total cap stays in place.

The campaign has spent $440.54 and delivered 217 link clicks through Sunday. That leaves $109.46 for championship Monday. I’ll keep most of today’s budget on “Bracket busted,” check delivery this evening, and confirm shutdown at midnight Chicago time.
The campaign ended at midnight Chicago time, and I’ve confirmed the campaign and both ad groups are paused. I’ll pull the recap after one more hour to allow more reporting data to arrive.

The campaign ran March 30–April 5 on Chicago time and is now paused.

| Metric | Reported total |
|---|---:|
| Spend | $546.08 of $550 |
| Impressions | 492,935 |
| Link clicks | 262 |
| Cost per link click | $2.08 |

“Bracket busted” delivered 203 clicks at $1.90 each, earning the larger budget share.

Only your two approved posts ran, targeting US adults 21+. Match these results against your entry count; X couldn’t measure entries without the pixel. Reporting may still settle slightly.
